title: Epistemology of Neuro-Virological Vulnerability and Clinical Autopoiesis: A Transdisciplinary Analysis of West Nile Virus Infection Across Immunopathogenesis, Atypical Manifestations, and the Ethics of Care
content: This  contribution  oﬀers  a  transdisciplinary  examination  of  West  Nile  virus  (WNV)  infection,  articulating  bio‐epidemiological  data  through  the lens  of  the  hermeneutics  of  care  and  embodied  cognition. Through an analysis of seroprevalence rates among blood, organ, cell, and tissue donors—with particular reference to the endemic Italian context—we highlight the critical issues surrounding iatrogenic  transmission  and  the  imperative  for  stringent  molecular  biosurveillance  protocols.  Furthermore, we dissect the mechanisms of immune evasion, susceptibility markers derived from systems  immunology,  and  therapeutic  perspectives  oﬀered  by  neutralizing  human  monoclonal  antibodies  isolated  from  convalescent  patients.  Finally,  the  investigation  extends  to  the  clinical  spectrum—from the diagnostic ICD‐10 code A92.3 to atypical manifestations such as acute ﬂaccid paralysis, myocarditis, and bullous dermatoses with keratinocyte tropism—interpreting the clinical trajectory from comatose states to functional recovery as a path of generative teleology and somatic proprioception.
